name: Matangini Hazra
contribution: A Gandhian organizer who joined the Civil Disobedience movement, took part in the Salt Satyagraha and anti-chowkidari-tax campaigns, and later led a large procession during the Quit India movement.
context: Born into a poor peasant family in Hogla near Tamluk, Matangini Hazra entered anti-colonial activism through local mass politics. She was arrested in 1932 for violating the salt law and again during the anti-chowkidari-tax campaign before becoming known as ‘Gandhi Buri’.
impact: On 29 September 1942, at age 72, she led a procession of thousands, mostly women, toward government offices in Tamluk. Police firing killed her as she continued to hold the national flag, making her a lasting symbol of women’s participation and sacrifice in the Quit India movement.
highlight: Gandhian leader who was killed while leading a Quit India procession in Tamluk in 1942.
seoTitle: Matangini Hazra: Gandhian Leader of the Quit India Movement
seoDescription: Learn about Matangini Hazra, the Bengal Gandhian who joined the Salt Satyagraha and was killed while leading a Quit India procession in Tamluk in 1942.
shortAnswer: Matangini Hazra was a Gandhian anti-colonial leader who led a Quit India procession in Tamluk and was killed by police firing on 29 September 1942.

faq.question: What is Matangini Hazra known for?
faq.answer: She is known for leading a large Quit India procession in Tamluk on 29 September 1942 and dying in police firing while holding the national flag.

faq.question: What was Matangini Hazra’s earlier activism?
faq.answer: She joined the 1932 Civil Disobedience and Salt Satyagraha campaigns, was arrested for violating the salt law, and later took part in the anti-chowkidari-tax movement.
